title: Old-Fashioned Beef Stew
summary: Classic red wine beef stew with carrots and potatoes. Mostly hands-off simmering.

steps.title: Coat the beef
steps.text: Mix the flour and pepper in a bowl and toss the beef in it until every piece is coated.

steps.title: Brown in batches
steps.text: Heat 3 tsp of the oil in a large pot. Brown the beef a few pieces at a time, turning until browned on all sides, about 5 minutes a batch. Don't crowd the pot; add more oil between batches as needed.

steps.title: Deglaze
steps.text: Take out the beef. Add the vinegar and wine and cook over medium-high, scraping up the browned bits.

steps.title: Start the simmer
steps.text: Return the beef, add the broth and bay leaves, bring to a boil, then drop to a slow simmer.

steps.title: Simmer until tender
steps.text: Cover and cook until the beef is tender, skimming the surface now and then.

steps.title: Onions and carrots
steps.text: Add the onion and carrots, cover, and simmer.

steps.title: Potatoes
steps.text: Add the potatoes and simmer until all the vegetables are tender. Add broth or water if it looks dry.

steps.title: Season and serve
steps.text: Season with salt and more pepper to taste, and pull the bay leaves.

notes: As written this serves 4 from 1 lb of beef; NYT says it doubles or triples well, so plan on 2.5x for the family (about 2.5 lb beef). Compare with the house wine-and-whiskey Burgundy stew.
